provenance.locus: Section 2 (The Soar Architecture) and Section 2.3 (Preferences and Operator Selection), per the real, confirmed DOI record (10.1016/0004-3702(87)90050-6, Artificial Intelligence 33(1):1-64) and a real secondary-source summary (Murdock 1997 / Davies 2000, jimdavies.org/summaries/laird1987.html, accessed live this session), which confirms: SOAR's core commitments include 'the use of explicit preferences to guide processing' and 'the definition of subgoals as responses to automatically detected impasses' -- i.e. preference-based operator selection with impasse-triggered subgoaling is a real, secondary-source-confirmed architectural fact, not an invented mechanism.
provenance.notes: The PDF at /Users/sac/Documents/Papers/AI_LLM/Laird-Newell-Rosenbloom-1987-SOAR-AIJ.pdf contains the Hearsay-II paper (Erman et al. 1980, Computing Surveys Vol.12 No.2), not the SOAR paper -- confirmed, and multiple later attempts this session to retrieve a real copy of Laird et al. 1987 (DTIC accessions ADA188742/ADA205407, CMU KiltHub, ResearchGate, Semantic Scholar) were all blocked (403s / site-permission restrictions), so page-level primary-source verification remains unavailable. extraction=secondary-source (upgraded from citation-only) because real secondary-source content WAS retrieved and read live this session (jimdavies.org's summary) and used to ground the architectural claims above -- but a specific verbatim quote with a page citation ('p.17: "If there is a single operator with a best preference ... it is selected."') that a prior version of this fixture asserted was never actually verified against the primary text and has been removed rather than left standing as if confirmed. The eight-puzzle domain and preference-hierarchy mechanism remain algorithmically consistent with both the real secondary-source description and this repo's own soar.rs implementation (confirmed by direct source-reading earlier this session: real preference symbols best/worst/require/prohibit/better-than, impasse detection, bounded subgoaling).
